question:
In the given figure AB and CD are two parallel chords of a circle with center O and radius 5 cm. Also AB = 8 cm and CD = 6 cm. If OP ⊥ AB and OQ ⊥ CD, determine the length of PQ:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7ffab13b50233d24a7ae954e493b7549f3b5aa76d4ac47f952c2a540fda0f6a2.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the common Pythagorean triplet (3, 4, 5) for a circle of radius 5 cm:

The perpendicular distance from the center to the chord of length 8 cm (half is 4 cm) is 3 cm.

The perpendicular distance from the center to the chord of length 6 cm (half is 3 cm) is 4 cm.

Since the difference (1 cm) is not in the options, the chords must lie on opposite sides of the center.

Total distance PQ = 3 + 4 = 7 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the circle (OA = OC) = 5 cm

Length of chord AB = 8 cm and chord CD = 6 cm

OP ⊥ AB and OQ ⊥ CD

**Formula Used:**

A perpendicular drawn from the center to a chord bisects the chord.

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

**Calculations:**

⇒ AP = AB ÷ 2 = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm

⇒ CQ = CD ÷ 2 = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm

In right-angled ΔOAP:

⇒ OP² + AP² = OA²

⇒ OP² + 4² = 5²

⇒ OP = √(25 − 16) = √9 = 3 cm

In right-angled ΔOCQ:

⇒ OQ² + CQ² = OC²

⇒ OQ² + 3² = 5²

⇒ OQ = √(25 − 9) = √16 = 4 cm

Since the chords are parallel and the answers provided only match the sum, they lie on opposite sides of the center O.

⇒ Total length PQ = OP + OQ

⇒ PQ = 3 + 4 = 7 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 7 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chord Properties

Equal chords are equidistant from the center of the circle, and conversely, chords equidistant from the center are equal in length.

Distance Between Parallel Chords

When two parallel chords lie on opposite sides of the center, the distance between them is the sum of their perpendicular distances. If they are on the same side, the distance is their difference.

Pythagorean Triplets

Common Pythagorean triplets like (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (8, 15, 17) frequently appear in circle and geometry problems to speed up calculations without calculating squares.
